arml-2014-superrelay-01.title: Common ratio
arml-2014-superrelay-01.body:
$a_{20}=r^6a_{14}$, so $r^6=\frac{2^3}{2^{21}}=2^{-18}$. For a real ratio, $r=\pm\frac18$, and $a_{21}=r\,a_{20}=\pm1$; the intended (positive) ratio $r=\frac18$ gives $a_{21}=1$.

**Answer: 1**

arml-2014-superrelay-02.title: Tangent is perpendicular to radius
arml-2014-superrelay-02.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 1, which is 1.)*


The centres are $LO=4T-T=3T$ apart, and $LE\perp OE$ with $LE=T$. So $OE=\sqrt{(3T)^2-T^2}=2\sqrt2\,T=2\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt2$**

arml-2014-superrelay-03.title: Pythagoras
arml-2014-superrelay-03.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 2, which is $2\sqrt2$.)*


The first leg is $T^2=8$. With hypotenuse $c$: $64+(c-2)^2=c^2\implies 68=4c\implies c=17$. The triangle is $8$-$15$-$17$ with perimeter $40$.

**Answer: 40**

arml-2014-superrelay-04.title: Eliminate x
arml-2014-superrelay-04.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 3, which is 40.)*


$T$ times the first equation minus the second: $(9T-T-1)y=17T-T-2$, i.e. $(8T-1)y=2(8T-1)$, so $y=2$ (as $T\ne\frac18$). Then $x=17-18=-1$ and $20x+14y=-20+28=8$.

**Answer: 8**

arml-2014-superrelay-05.title: Vieta and two points
arml-2014-superrelay-05.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 4, which is 8.)*


The product of the roots is $\frac ca=T$, so $c=Ta$. Then $4a-2b+Ta=20$ and $a+b+Ta=14$. Adding twice the second to the first: $6a+3Ta=48$, so $a=\frac{16}{T+2}=\frac{16}{10}=\frac85$.

**Answer: $\frac85$**

arml-2014-superrelay-06.title: Distance in the complex plane
arml-2014-superrelay-06.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 5, which is $\frac85$.)*


$z_1-z_2=14+(5-K)i$ and $15T=24$, so we need $196+(K-5)^2\ge576$, i.e. $(K-5)^2\ge380$. Since $19^2=361<380\le400=20^2$, and $K$ is a positive integer ($5-K\le-20$ is needed, as $5-K\ge20$ is impossible), $K\ge25$.

**Answer: 25**

arml-2014-superrelay-07.title: Inclusion–exclusion
arml-2014-superrelay-07.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 6, which is 25.)*


Charlie is next to Chris in $(T-1)\cdot2\cdot(T-2)!=2(T-1)!$ of the $T!$ lineups; the same for Abby. Both happen when Charlie is in the middle of a block of three: $(T-2)\cdot2\cdot(T-3)!=2(T-2)!$ lineups. So
$$P=\frac{4(T-1)!-2(T-2)!}{T!}=\frac{2(2T-3)}{T(T-1)}=\frac{2\cdot47}{25\cdot24}=\frac{47}{300}.$$

**Answer: $\frac{47}{300}$**

arml-2014-superrelay-07.title: Condition on Charlie's position
arml-2014-superrelay-07.body:
If Charlie is at an end ($2$ of $25$ positions), he has one neighbour, who is Chris or Abby with probability $\frac2{24}$. Otherwise he has two neighbours, and the probability neither is Chris or Abby is $\frac{22}{24}\cdot\frac{21}{23}$. So
$$P=\frac2{25}\cdot\frac1{12}+\frac{23}{25}\left(1-\frac{22\cdot21}{24\cdot23}\right)=\frac{2}{300}+\frac{23}{25}\cdot\frac{90}{552}=\frac{2}{300}+\frac{45}{300}=\frac{47}{300}.$$

**Answer: $\frac{47}{300}$**

arml-2014-superrelay-08.title: Sum formula
arml-2014-superrelay-08.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $A$ was the answer to problem 7, $\frac{47}{300}$, and $B$ the answer to problem 9, $\frac{12}{169}$.)*

$\sin(\alpha+\beta)+\sin(\alpha-\beta)=2\sin\alpha\cos\beta=2AB=\frac{2\cdot47\cdot12}{300\cdot169}=\frac{94}{4225}$.

**Answer: $\frac{94}{4225}$**

arml-2014-superrelay-09.title: Maximise a quadratic
arml-2014-superrelay-09.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 10, which is 13.)*


$V(r)=\frac13\pi r^2(T-r^2)$. With $x=r^2$, $x(T-x)$ is maximised at $x=\frac T2$, so $V=\frac13\pi\cdot\frac{T^2}4=\frac{\pi T^2}{12}$ and $\frac\pi V=\frac{12}{T^2}=\frac{12}{169}$.

**Answer: $\frac{12}{169}$**

arml-2014-superrelay-10.title: Combine logs
arml-2014-superrelay-10.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 11, which is 650.)*


$2=\log100$, so $\log T=\log\frac{100k}{2}=\log(50k)$, giving $k=\frac T{50}=13$.

**Answer: 13**

arml-2014-superrelay-11.title: Difference of speeds
arml-2014-superrelay-11.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 12, which is 100.)*


With distance $D$: $\frac DT-\frac D{T+30}=1.5$, so $\frac{30D}{T(T+30)}=\frac32$ and $D=\frac{T(T+30)}{20}=\frac{100\cdot130}{20}=650$.

**Answer: 650 miles**

arml-2014-superrelay-12.title: Exponent arithmetic
arml-2014-superrelay-12.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 13, which is 9.)*


The expression is $10^{\frac{T^2-T}{T}\cdot\frac14}=10^{\frac{T-1}4}=10^2=100$.

**Answer: 100**

arml-2014-superrelay-13.title: Short diagonal
arml-2014-superrelay-13.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 14, which is 3.)*


$SU=RE=\sqrt T$. $BE$ skips one vertex ($R$), so it is a short diagonal: in $\triangle BRE$ with $BR=RE=\sqrt T$ and $\angle R=120^\circ$, $BE=\sqrt3\cdot\sqrt T$. So the product is $\sqrt{3T}\cdot T=T\sqrt{3T}=3\cdot3=9$.

**Answer: 9**

arml-2014-superrelay-14.title: Multiplication principle
arml-2014-superrelay-14.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 15, which is 70.)*


There are $4\cdot3\cdot2\cdot K=24K$ varieties; $24K\ge70$ first holds at $K=3$.

**Answer: 3**

arml-2014-superrelay-15.title: Cancel the common factor
arml-2014-superrelay-15.body:
$14\mid20N\iff7\mid10N\iff7\mid N$, and $20\mid14N\iff10\mid7N\iff10\mid N$. So $N$ is a multiple of $\mathrm{lcm}(7,10)=70$.

**Answer: 70**
